semantic_correction.stem: During routine assessment of a client with a nontunneled central venous catheter, the RN finds that the transparent dressing is damp and one edge has lifted from the skin. The insertion site is not actively bleeding. Which action is most appropriate?

options.A: Reinforce the lifted edge with tape and leave the dressing in place until the next scheduled central-line dressing change.
options.B: Replace the damp, loose dressing now using aseptic technique and the facility's central-line dressing-change protocol.
options.C: Dry the outside of the dressing with sterile gauze and continue using it if the insertion site has no redness or drainage.
options.D: Remove the central venous catheter because a damp or loose dressing means the line should be considered infected.

semantic_correction.rationale: Current CDC intravascular-catheter infection-prevention recommendations state that a catheter-site dressing should be replaced when it becomes damp, loosened, or visibly soiled. CDC also emphasizes hand hygiene and appropriate aseptic technique during catheter maintenance and dressing changes. The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes accessing and/or maintaining central venous access devices and providing care for clients with central venous access devices under Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies. Because this transparent dressing is both damp and partially lifted, B is the uniquely appropriate action: replace it now using aseptic technique and the facility's catheter-care protocol. A leaves a compromised dressing in place. C attempts to dry rather than replace a dressing whose integrity is already lost. D incorrectly equates a compromised dressing with proven catheter infection and unnecessarily removes the device. Therefore B is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Replace a central-line dressing promptly when it becomes damp, loose, or visibly soiled, using aseptic technique and the applicable catheter-care protocol rather than reinforcing, drying, or automatically removing the catheter.

Rebuilt the item around explicit NCSBN central-venous-access maintenance content and current CDC catheter-dressing guidance. Removed the prior absolute-word distractor cue.

scope_exclusions.automatic_catheter_removal: Not endorsed. A damp or loose dressing requires dressing replacement but does not by itself establish catheter-related bloodstream infection or mandate catheter removal.
scope_exclusions.specific_antiseptic_for_every_client: Not tested. CDC generally recommends chlorhexidine-alcohol for central-line dressing changes with alternatives when contraindicated; the item appropriately refers to the facility catheter-care protocol rather than universalizing one product.
scope_exclusions.active_bleeding_or_oozing: Explicitly excluded in the stem. CDC may favor gauze while bleeding/oozing persists; this item tests dressing integrity rather than bleeding management.
scope_exclusions.routine_schedule_override: The dressing is already damp and loose, so replacement is clinically indicated regardless of the next routine scheduled change.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0776 tests contamination of a critical sterile field during central-line dressing change. V2-Q0622 tests malfunctioning equipment removal/reporting. V2-Q0824 tests hemodialysis AV-fistula protection. V2-Q0827 tests recognition and replacement of an already damp/loose central-line dressing. Targeted repository search for damp/loose central-line dressing replacement returned no matching item before staging.

option_audit.A: Plausible temporary-securement response but leaves a dressing whose integrity has already been compromised.
option_audit.B: Correct. It follows CDC guidance to replace a damp or loose catheter dressing using appropriate aseptic maintenance technique.
option_audit.C: Plausible moisture-management response but drying the exterior does not restore dressing integrity or adherence.
option_audit.D: Plausible infection-prevention concern but overinterprets dressing compromise as confirmed infection requiring catheter removal.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. The stem explicitly states that the dressing is damp and an edge has lifted, meeting CDC replacement criteria. B alone replaces the compromised dressing without inventing infection or unnecessary catheter removal. A/C preserve a compromised dressing; D overreacts by removing the catheter.
